key_insight: Identity-paired progressive depth training (IP-PDT) avoids initialization shock by adding forward/inverse layer pairs that start as identity, revealing that optimization can keep improving even after the expressible circuit saturates.
engineering_relevance: For hardware-efficient VQAs, IP-PDT offers a practical training schedule that reduces CNOT overhead, stabilizes depth growth, and can improve convergence on near-term quantum devices.
method: Train shallow-first, then append identity-paired forward/inverse blocks instead of raw new layers.
Use the cancellation of adjacent CNOT rings so added depth mainly increases local rotation parameters, not entangling cost.
Apply an acceptance-based continuation rule to keep energy monotonically improving during depth growth.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical guarantees, including a reachable-set saturation theorem, monotone energy under the acceptance rule, and resource analysis showing lower total gate cost than baselines.
watch_item: The method relies on careful layer-acceptance and cancellation structure, so performance may depend on ansatz design and precise circuit implementation.
paper_title: Identity-Paired Progressive Depth Training: When Trainability Persists Beyond Expressibility
